title: Run market-hours Nautilus strategy paper-submit validation

acceptance_criteria: During regular market hours, a bounded paper-submit run uses AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy and AlpacaExecutionClientFactory for submission; accepted/rejected/denied order events update durable strategy state; broker account/orders are checked after the run; any accepted smoke orders are canceled unless explicitly left open; logs and operator status show no unmanaged exposure or duplicate submission.

title: Remove legacy Alpaca account-engine entry loop
description: Delete the direct account-engine entry submission path once the Nautilus strategy path owns admission, submission, durable state, and evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Direct account-engine entry submission code is removed; displaced entry-only helpers in options_engine.rs are deleted or moved to their true owner; ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED is removed or replaced by the normal runtime submit gate; docs and AGENTS guidance no longer describe the account engine as the order-capable entry owner; targeted live checks show the strategy path remains order-capable.
close_reason: Removed the legacy Alpaca account-engine entry loop. alpaca-options-engine is now management-only for existing entries; direct entry scan/decision/submission code and entry-only helper events were deleted from options_engine.rs/options_engine/events.rs, ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED and node_entry_submit_enabled were removed, and the option-chain live node now uses the normal ALPACA_SUBMIT runtime gate for Nautilus strategy submission readiness. Updated active Alpaca code comments/status naming away from account-engine entry ownership. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; git diff --check; bounded live-node smoke with ALPACA_SUBMIT=true and ALPACA_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS=0 acquired the runtime lease, emitted live_submit_readiness, registered the Nautilus option-chain actor and AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy, scanned SPY 2026-07-06, selected a call_credit candidate, blocked it with risk_max_open_orders current=0 limit=0 before broker submission, shut down cleanly, and released the lease. Post-run alpaca-operator-status showed account ACTIVE, trading_blocked=false, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current, and service inactive. Actual market-hours submit validation remains tracked by nt-9l3.8.

title: Prove strategy admission parity against the account engine
description: Prove that AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy applies the same entry-admission constraints as the legacy account-engine loop before enabling the strategy as the order-capable path.
acceptance_criteria: The strategy refuses every entry the account engine would refuse using the same persisted strategy state, daily/active/fleet limits, open-order count, candidate-leg position/order checks, same-underlying position/order checks, account-tradability blocks, permission memory, and reason strings; cutover proof or targeted live dry-run evidence shows selected, blocked, and dry-run decisions match the old loop.
notes: Implemented parity plumbing: strategy admission now includes startup Alpaca account-tradability reasons, uses shared persisted StrategyState/fleet/risk admission config, counts unique open broker order intents from Nautilus cache for max-open-orders parity instead of counting every cached leg, keeps candidate-leg and same-underlying position/order checks from Nautilus cache, and emits structured entry_decision operator events for kill-switch, outside-window, submission_disabled dry-runs, state_persistence_unhealthy, duplicate pending submission, and selected_but_blocked decisions. Existing Alpaca live library tests pass and the gated live-submit smoke proved readiness with no broker exposure. Remaining before closing: produce real selected/blocked/dry-run parity evidence against the account engine during a cutover proof or targeted live dry-run that yields a selected candidate; the latest SPY 2026-06-30 smoke had no ranked candidate, so it did not prove selected-candidate parity.
close_reason: Implemented and proved AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy admission parity against the legacy account-engine path. Shared admission now carries account-tradability reasons into the Nautilus strategy, applies the same persisted StrategyState/fleet/risk/daily limits, classifies candidate-leg and same-underlying broker conflicts from the Nautilus cache, counts open broker order intents for max-open-orders admission, and emits structured entry_decision evidence for dry-run and selected_but_blocked outcomes. Fixed option-chain trade-date derivation so daily risk state uses the configured market trade-date clock instead of stale quote slice timestamps; scan events now include trade_date. Live evidence: account engine dry-run and Nautilus strategy dry-run both selected SPY call_credit legs SPY260706C00743000/SPY260706C00745000 with reason submission_disabled; account engine selected-but-blocked and Nautilus strategy selected-but-blocked both selected the same legs and blocked with risk_max_open_orders current=0 limit=0. Live-submit-gated Nautilus proof acquired readiness/lease, startup reconciliation saw 0 orders/fills/positions, emitted live_submit_readiness, emitted selected_but_blocked, released the runtime lease, and post-run operator status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; git diff --check.

title: Complete strategy live-submit readiness and startup reconciliation
description: Make the AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy path safe to enable for live paper submission by requiring storage readiness, a live-submit lease, healthy persistence, and startup reconciliation of broker orders/positions/pending submissions.
acceptance_criteria: When ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED=true, the live node fails closed unless Postgres migrations are current, the state persistence sink is healthy, and an active account writer lease is held; startup reconciles broker orders, positions, pending or partially accepted entries, and persisted strategy state before submission can occur; persistence failure denies new entries and emits operator evidence; restart smoke proves no duplicate submit for pending/accepted broker state.
close_reason: Implemented live-submit readiness safeguards for the Alpaca Nautilus strategy path. Live submit now requires current Postgres migrations, an acquired runtime lease, a healthy state persistence sink, startup account-admission checks, and broker/state reconciliation before the node can submit. Shared broker/state reconciliation now blocks live submit on unmanaged positions, unmanaged open orders, or partial-position state. Persistence write/queue failures and runtime lease heartbeat loss mark the persistence handle unhealthy and emit operator evidence, so later entries are denied. Graceful live-node shutdown releases the runtime lease; crash safety still falls back to TTL. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; bounded live-submit-gated smoke with ALPACA_SUBMIT=true, ALPACA_OPTIONS_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_ENABLED=true, ALPACA_KILL_SWITCH=true acquired lease, emitted live_submit_readiness with storage_ready/lease_held/broker_state_reconciled, startup reconciliation saw 0 orders/fills/positions, exited cleanly, and emitted runtime_lease_released. Post-run operator status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations applied, and engine blocked by kill switch/submission-disabled container gates.

title: Add transactional Alpaca state event and snapshot write
description: Add a repository method that inserts one strategy state event and updates the strategy_state snapshot idempotently in one transaction.
acceptance_criteria: A synthetic accepted or rejected state mutation can persist event and snapshot atomically and tolerate duplicate event IDs.
close_reason: Added persist_strategy_state_mutation repository contract with typed StrategyStateMutation/StrategyStateWriteResult. The transaction inserts strategy_state_events idempotently, locks/version-updates strategy_state only for new events, records writer/run/last_event metadata, and supports expected-version conflicts. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, and a disposable /tmp Rust harness calling the public method against local Alpaca Postgres: first synthetic entry_accepted write returned Applied version 1, replay returned DuplicateEvent version 1. Verified the DB row had one event and matching snapshot metadata, then deleted the generated smoke account rows.

title: Wire Alpaca strategy-state persistence sink into live readiness
description: Wire a Nautilus-native async state persistence sink into the live node and gate paper submit on storage readiness, lease, and sink health.
acceptance_criteria: The strategy keeps in-memory protection immediately, persists accepted/rejected state through the sink, and refuses live submit when persistence is unhealthy.
close_reason: Wired live option-chain node readiness to require Postgres storage only when live entry submit is requested; it now checks required migration version, acquires and heartbeats a runtime_lease, loads storage-backed state, and passes a StrategyStatePersistenceHandle into AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy. The strategy refuses live entries when persistence is missing/unhealthy, keeps in-memory state updates immediate, and enqueues accepted plus terminal rejected/denied state mutations through the async sink. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, and a disposable /tmp harness against local Alpaca Postgres that acquired a lease, enqueued duplicate entry_accepted mutations through the public persistence handle, verified one event plus snapshot version 1 and lease row, then deleted the generated smoke rows.

title: Wire scanner and strategy evidence through async persistence sinks
description: Persist scanner and strategy evidence through explicit async sink/consumer boundaries instead of direct synchronous strategy callback writes or adapter-local one-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Scanner evidence, selected candidates, blocks, dry-runs, submissions, and relevant strategy decisions flow through bounded async persistence sinks; failures mark the sink unhealthy, deny live submissions when safety-critical, and emit operator evidence; scan math and candidate ranking remain pure and independent of persistence.
notes: 2026-06-27 discovery from nt-9l3.7 validation: bounded live-node smoke emits option_chain_opportunity_scan and entry_decision to stdout, but alpaca-operator-status reads only the configured operator log path; after the smoke broker/account state was flat, but last_scan did not surface the fresh live-node scan. Treat this as evidence-sink/log-capture scope, not entry-loop removal scope.
close_reason: Implemented bounded async candidate-ledger persistence for the Nautilus Alpaca live path. Option-chain scanner evidence now flows through CandidateLedgerPersistenceHandle as scanner_result and ranked candidate records; AlpacaOptionsEntryStrategy writes selected_candidate alerts for dry-run, blocked, skipped, and submitted decisions plus candidate_submit_rejected alerts for terminal reject/deny evidence. Live submit now fails closed when candidate-ledger persistence is absent or unhealthy, and runtime lease loss marks both state and candidate-ledger sinks unhealthy. The live node flushes candidate-ledger evidence before releasing the runtime lease. alpaca-operator-status now reads recent durable candidate-ledger records so last_scan and last_decision do not depend on stdout log capture. Duplicate selected-candidate alerts are suppressed per run while scanner/candidate records remain per scan. Validation: cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins; cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib; git diff --check; bounded live-node smoke with ALPACA_SUBMIT=true and ALPACA_MAX_OPEN_ORDERS=0 acquired readiness/lease, scanned SPY 2026-07-06, selected a call_credit candidate, blocked with risk_max_open_orders, flushed evidence, released the lease, and left the broker flat. alpaca-operator-status showed account ACTIVE, 0 open orders, 0 positions, storage migrations current, durable last_scan=scanner_result source=option_chain, and durable last_decision=selected_candidate action=selected_but_blocked reason=risk_max_open_orders. alpaca-candidate-alerts --dry-run with a 1-minute lookback showed exactly one eligible selected-candidate alert for the fresh run.

close_reason: Split nautilus-persistence into catalog-write, catalog-query, clickhouse-write, clickhouse-read, clickhouse-catalog, clickhouse-migrations, clickhouse, and live-dual-write features. Live warehouse paths now use catalog-write + clickhouse-write without streaming/DataFusion, while CLI/operator paths keep the full clickhouse feature for migrations/backfill/validation. Validation: cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --no-default-features --features live-dual-write; cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --no-default-features --features clickhouse; cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --no-default-features --features catalog-write; cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --no-default-features --features clickhouse-write; cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --no-default-features --features python; cargo check -p nautilus-data --no-default-features --features warehouse-clickhouse; cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --no-default-features --features live,warehouse-clickhouse --bin alpaca-options-engine --bin alpaca-operator-status --bin alpaca-check-account-orders --bin alpaca-option-chain-scan-live-node; cargo check -p nautilus-cli; cargo tree -p nautilus-alpaca --no-default-features --features live,warehouse-clickhouse -i datafusion failed because datafusion is absent; same absence confirmed for nautilus-data warehouse-clickhouse, nautilus-persistence live-dual-write, catalog-write, and clickhouse-write; cargo fmt --check; git diff --check.

title: Speed up Alpaca Docker rollout builds
description: Reduce normal Alpaca Docker rollout compile time by adding BuildKit Cargo cache mounts, introducing a faster rollout Cargo profile, and splitting normal runtime binaries from optional operator/tool binaries.
acceptance_criteria: Dockerfile uses persistent BuildKit caches for Cargo registry/git/target and copies built artifacts out of the cache mount; normal Docker builds default to a faster rollout profile while production release remains available by build arg; optional tools can be excluded from the default runtime image; compose config remains valid and a Docker build validates the default path.
close_reason: Implemented BuildKit Cargo registry/git/target caches, release-rollout default profile, and runtime/tools image split. Validation: docker compose config passed; git diff --check passed; default docker compose build alpaca-options completed and exported nautilus-alpaca:local; warmed rerun completed Rust build in 3m38s; slim image runs alpaca-options-engine --help, includes four core binaries, and excludes alpaca-compare-option-chain-scan.

title: Align ClickHouse warehouse database ownership
description: Live validation shows quote rows are stored in market.quote_ticks while the runtime config advertises CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE=warehouse. Clean this up so the repo-level warehouse has one explicit database ownership model: either the configured database owns quote tables or the config is renamed/removed if market is intentionally canonical. Also ensure operator validation queries are bounded enough to run under the self-hosted 2 GiB ClickHouse limit.
acceptance_criteria: Database naming is coherent between config, migrations, writer, reader, docs, and compose; no hard-coded market database remains unless it is the documented canonical database; live validation can verify recent quote rows without full-table aggregates exceeding the ClickHouse memory cap.
notes: Aligned ClickHouse ownership so market-data tables are canonical under market (default CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE/CLICKHOUSE_DB=market) and warehouse is reserved for operator metadata in warehouse.schema_migrations. Added explicit Rust constants for market quote table and warehouse metadata table, bootstrap migrations through default DB so fresh ClickHouse can create market/warehouse, and require bounded start_ns/end_ns for ClickHouse QuoteTick reads with event_date partition pruning. Validated cargo fmt -p nautilus-persistence -p nautilus-cli, cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --features clickhouse --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-cli, cargo check -p nautilus-data --features warehouse-clickhouse --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-live --features warehouse-clickhouse --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live,warehouse-clickhouse --bins, docker compose configs for warehouse/alpaca, live warehouse health/migrate/quote-smoke with CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE=market, unbounded validate-quotes fail-fast, and direct ClickHouse table ownership check for market.quote_ticks plus warehouse.schema_migrations.
close_reason: ClickHouse warehouse ownership is aligned: market owns quote tables, warehouse owns migration metadata, defaults/docs/compose match, and bounded validation was live-verified against the running self-hosted ClickHouse.

title: Fix same-day option expiry handling in live option-chain manager
description: During 2026-06-26 market-hours live validation, the host live option-chain node subscribed to SPY 2026-06-26 contracts but immediately logged that the series ALPACA:SPY:USD:2026-06-26T00:00:00Z was expired and dropped same-day quotes. This suggests option expiry is represented at midnight UTC for instruments that should remain tradable through the market session. Keep separate from the sell_short parser fix.
acceptance_criteria: A market-hours 0DTE option-chain subscription does not drop live quotes as expired before the exchange close/actual contract expiration; future-expiry behavior remains unchanged; targeted live or fixture-backed validation passes.
notes:
Live validation on 2026-06-26 avoided the 0DTE drop by overriding ALPACA_OPTION_CHAIN_EXPIRY=2026-06-30. With the future expiry, the live node subscribed to 6 SPY option instruments and flushed quote data successfully; the same-day expiry issue remains isolated to 0DTE handling.
Verified Alpaca /v2/options/contracts live response for SPY 2026-06-26 returns expiration_date as date-only (YYYY-MM-DD), not a timestamp. Updated adapter parsing to preserve RFC3339 timestamps if Alpaca ever returns them, otherwise normalize date-only option expirations to 16:15 America/New_York. Same-day live-node validation for SPY 2026-06-26 built series ALPACA:SPY:USD:2026-06-26T20:15:00Z, subscribed 354 cached instruments / 6 active instruments, emitted option_chain_opportunity_scan snapshots, and did not drop quotes as expired.
close_reason: Fixed Alpaca date-only option expiration normalization and validated same-day live option-chain quotes no longer drop as expired before close.

title: Support Alpaca sell_short side during mass-status reconciliation
description: Live Alpaca option-chain node reconciliation currently warns: failed to parse Alpaca payload: unsupported Alpaca order side: sell_short. This did not block market-data dual-write validation, but it weakens startup order/position reconciliation and should be fixed in the Alpaca adapter parser using Nautilus-native order-side semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A live or fixture-backed mass-status payload containing side=sell_short parses without warning and maps to the correct Nautilus side semantics; targeted Alpaca adapter check passes.
notes: Fixed order_side_from_alpaca to map Alpaca action-style order side values to Nautilus OrderSide: buy_to_cover/buy_to_open/buy_to_close => Buy, sell_short/sell_to_open/sell_to_close => Sell. Host live-node validation during market hours reached LiveNode startup reconciliation and succeeded: received 739 orders, 428 fills, 8 positions; reconciliation succeeded with no unsupported sell_short warning. Dual-write was disabled for that host parser validation to avoid adding storage rows.
close_reason: Alpaca order-side parser now accepts sell_short and related action-style side values. Validated with cargo fmt, cargo test -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --lib, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live,warehouse-clickhouse --bins, and a live host option-chain node startup reconciliation with no sell_short parse warning.

title: Build catalog to ClickHouse backfill proof
description: Build the first catalog-backed warehouse backfill operation for QuoteTick data with row counts and run audit output.
acceptance_criteria: A sampled catalog date and instrument range loads into ClickHouse and validates counts through the warehouse operator.
close_reason: Added warehouse backfill-quotes operator path backed by ParquetDataCatalog and ClickHouse QuoteTick writer; validated cargo fmt/check/build, live backfill from 64-bit catalog sample with catalog_rows=9500 written_rows=9500 warehouse_rows=9500, and direct ClickHouse count for ingest run.

title: Slim Postgres market-data cache after warehouse proof
description: Retire or narrow Postgres market-data-shaped cache usage after catalog and ClickHouse cover those datasets.
acceptance_criteria: Postgres keeps operational state, evidence, outcomes, leases, and small manifests only; bulk market data and scanner feature time series move to catalog or ClickHouse.
close_reason: Retired the Postgres backtest_market_cache path after ClickHouse proof. Removed Alpaca options-backtest Postgres market-cache reads/writes and the storage market_cache module/export, added forward sqlx migration 202606230003_drop_backtest_market_cache.sql, and updated active docs/checklists to keep market-data-shaped caches in catalog/ClickHouse rather than Postgres. Validated with cargo fmt -p nautilus-alpaca, cargo check -p nautilus-alpaca --features live --bins, cargo check -p nautilus-cli, cargo check -p nautilus-persistence --features clickhouse, local Alpaca Postgres migration application via alpaca-sync-strategy-state proving backtest_market_cache is absent and migration 202606230003 is recorded, ClickHouse warehouse migrate/health/quote-smoke via nautilus CLI, docker compose warehouse smoke, and direct ClickHouse row check for source live-validation.

title: Add warehouse read validation and cutover flag
description: Add explicit catalog versus ClickHouse validation for selected dataset ranges and a simple read-source flag for controlled cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can validate a supported range, switch reads to clickhouse mode, and roll back to catalog mode by configuration.
close_reason: Added repo-level QuoteTick validate-quotes operator command, market-data read-source flag parsing, and selected-source QuoteTick read helper. Validated cargo fmt/check/build plus live catalog-vs-ClickHouse validation for 9500 rows with NAUTILUS_MARKET_DATA_READ_SOURCE=clickhouse and rollback to catalog.
